guide.summary: Moorish fortresses, the cathedral and Picasso, Pompidou and Thyssen museums, plus tapas bars, tasting-menu dinners, coffee, a bakery and cocktail terraces, all checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Several sights are free on Sunday afternoons: the Alcazaba and Gibralfaro from 14:00, the Carmen Thyssen, Museo Ruso and Casa Natal Picasso from 16:00, and the Museo Picasso Málaga in its last two hours.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Museo Carmen Thyssen, Colección del Museo Ruso and Museo Revello de Toro close on Mondays, and the Centre Pompidou Málaga closes on Tuesdays. Palodú is closed Sunday to Tuesday, and El Mesón de Cervantes lists service only Wednesday to Monday.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: One combined ticket covers the Alcazaba and Castillo de Gibralfaro for €10.00 (€7.00 each separately). From 1 November both run 9:00-18:00, with last entry at 17:00.

toolkit.label: Booking rules
toolkit.copy: Kaleja asks for a card to confirm a booking and charges €100 per guest for no-shows or cancellations under 24 hours, holding tables for 15 minutes. El Pimpi takes reservation requests by phone or at reservas@elpimpi.com.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: The Catedral de Málaga asks visitors to dress with decorum and suspends tourist visits during weekend liturgies. Its roof visit means about 200 steps on a narrow spiral stair, with tripods, backpacks and food not allowed.

guide.dek: Do the hilltop fortresses in the morning, keep Sunday afternoons for free museum entry, and check closing days before you book dinner.
intro: Start at the top. The Alcazaba, at Calle Alcazabilla 2, and the Castillo de Gibralfaro above it are run by the city on one combined ticket of €10.00. From 1 November to 31 March both open 9:00 to 18:00, with last entry an hour before closing, and both are free every Sunday from 14:00. To reach Gibralfaro you can take EMT bus line 35 or walk up Paseo de Don Juan Temboury in about 20 minutes. At the foot of the Alcazaba, the Junta de Andalucía runs the Teatro Romano free of charge, closed on Mondays.

Picasso runs through the old town. The Museo Picasso Málaga on Calle San Agustín opens every day; from November to February it closes at 18:00, and it opens "Munch-Picasso" from 30 October 2026 to 28 February 2027. Entry is €13, free in the last two hours on Sundays. A few streets away, the Museo Casa Natal Picasso on Plaza de la Merced opens daily 9:30 to 20:00 for €3, with free entry on Sundays from 16:00. The Catedral de Málaga on Calle Molina Lario sells audioguide tickets for €10 and offers daily guided visits to its roof.

For modern art, the Centre Pompidou Málaga on Muelle Uno opens 9:30 to 20:00 but closes on Tuesdays; "TO OPEN EYES" runs until 17 January 2027. The Museo Carmen Thyssen Málaga closes on Mondays and shows "¡Olé! El mito de lo español a través de Andalucía" until 21 February 2027. Out at Tabacalera, the Colección del Museo Ruso charges €4 and shows Mijaíl Glinka until 31 January 2027. With children, the MIMMA music museum on Calle Beatas charges €6 for adults, and La Concepción botanical garden opens Tuesday to Sunday, closing at 17:30 from October to March.

Eat and drink around Calle Granada. El Pimpi, founded in 1971, serves non-stop from noon until midnight, and until 00:30 on Fridays and Saturdays. Antigua Casa de Guardia on the Alameda Principal, founded in 1840, closes at 15:00 on Sundays. For a set-piece dinner, Palodú offers menus at €115 and €135 per person and closes Sunday to Tuesday, while Kaleja requires a card to confirm a booking. Morning coffee is easy at Santa Coffee in Soho, which roasts its own beans and opens at 8:00 on weekdays.
summaryCards: Buy the €10 combined Alcazaba and Gibralfaro ticket, then walk down to the Teatro Romano and the Museo Picasso Málaga.
Have coffee at Santa Coffee in Soho from 8:00 on weekdays, then spend a few hours in La Concepción botanical garden, open Tuesday to Sunday.
Check closing days: the Centre Pompidou shuts on Tuesdays, several museums on Mondays, Palodú Sunday to Tuesday, and Kaleja charges €100 per guest for late cancellations.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several places publish hours but no dated 2026 content (Antigua Casa de Guardia, El Mesón de Cervantes, Casa Lola and Pez Lola, Santa Coffee, Museo Revello de Toro), and the cathedral's hours table carries no year. Kaleja, Chester & Punk and La Terraza at the Catalonia Molina Lario publish no opening hours; Palodú publishes only closing days; La Canasta gives hours only for its Avenida de la Aurora shop. Playa de la Malagueta has no street address, only coordinates on the city page. The Mercado Central de Atarazanas is left out because no official page could be found. The Museo de Málaga, CAC Málaga, Casa Aranda, La Recova, the Museo Automovilístico, Museo Alborania, Café Central, Los Mellizos and the Hotel Larios terrace could not be read because of certificate errors, 403/520 responses or timeouts. Those failures are not evidence of closure.
